A '''bipedal species''' lived in [[the galaxy]] during the [[Imperial Era]]. A [[species]] of tall, thin-necked beings, at least one member resided in a [[Mapuzo mining village|mining village]] on [[Mapuzo]]<ref name="Kenobi Part III">{{Kenobi|Part III}}</ref> in [[9 BBY]],<ref name="Kenobi Date">{{KenobiDate|III}}</ref> while another was present on the [[Spur Orbiting Market]]<ref name="Bounty Hunters 6" /> in [[3 ABY]].<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Bounty Hunters 6|''Bounty Hunters'' 6]] to [[3 ABY]].</ref> That individual was on the [[space station]] during an altercation between an [[Unidentified Arcona bounty hunter|Arcona bounty hunter]] and the [[cyborg]] [[Beilert Valance]].<ref name="Bounty Hunters 6" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I love trying to find ways of pushing the form and hiding the performer. I squeezed Aiden Cook ''[sic]'' into the cages of Bobbajo on ''The Force Awakens'' and this time he's hidden in the load on this long-necked alien's shoulder.|Jake Lunt Davies|<ref name="Art of TROS">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker]]''</ref>}}
[[File:LongNeckedSpecies-BountyHunters6.jpg|left|150px|thumb|A member of this species on the Spur Orbiting Market.]]
The species was originally designed by artist [[Jake Lunt Davies]] for the [[2019]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']], the final film of the [[sequel trilogy]]. Davies desired to push the form of creature design with this species, creating a concept that would hide the performer in the props carried on the creature's back. To operate the head, Davies envisioned the performer sticking their arm straight up through the costume's neck.<ref name="Art of TROS" />

The design made it to the production phase of the film, with performer [[Aidan Cook]] portraying the individual on set.<ref name="Art of TROS" /> Ultimately, however, the character was cut from the final film.<ref name="Episode IX">{{Film|IX}}</ref> A member of the species was later included in the background of a panel of the [[Bounty Hunters 6|sixth issue]] of the [[2020]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunters]]'', illustrated by [[Paolo Villanelli]].<ref name="Bounty Hunters 6" />

The costume eventually made its live action debut in the [[Part III|third episode]] of [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi|''Obi-Wan Kenobi'']], a [[2022]] [[Disney+]] limited series.<ref name="Kenobi Part III" /> The creature was performed by [[Morgana Ignis]]. During breaks while shooting, Ignis broke into impromptu dance numbers while in-costume, eliciting laughter and applause from lead actor [[Ewan McGregor]].<ref name="Ignis Tweet">{{Twitter|IgnisTwote|status/1532032793277935617|[[Morgana Ignis]]|date=2022-06-01|quote=Another hidden Morgana on today's episode of #Kenobi!! I puppeteered this merchant buddy on the right! They were a really cool creature and I made them dance and bow for Ewan between shots, which got me some hella validating laughs and applause from Obi Wan 😜 #StarWars|archivedate=20220601161457}}</ref>
